title: Accumulating component upgrades and automatic grade promotion
status: Planned implementation requirements; not a claim of released gameplay. Published player documentation and release notes identify available features.
request: Applied upgrades increase actual compatible component stats until the next grade template is met, then promote the same component and retain excess progress. Advanced II shields can reach Elite.
precedence: Real stat-based promotion replaces display-only grading and incompatible lifetime caps. Purchases separately obey the full prerequisite graph; promotion never fabricates purchase receipts. New monotonic templates must preserve saved actual strength and accumulated value.
names: Canonical shield display names use Intermediate and Intermediate II, following the latest user purchase sequence. Intermediary/Intermediary II and old Pulse/Mining/Beam/Military/Capital labels are legacy aliases. Equipment Elite is distinct from commander combat rank.
component_state: Each fitted/stored component has a stable instance ID, compatible family, authoritative grade, immutable family base/template version, accumulated intrinsic stat improvements and feature modules, plus applied-item receipt IDs. Grade is derived/reconciled when a valid upgrade transaction changes stats, not incremented each frame or inferred from a mutable display string.
upgrade_transaction: Inspect a recovered compatible upgrade and show actual before/after values, any newly enabled feature, resulting grade and progress to next grade. Ordinary upgrades can be fitted immediately after salvage, including in space; alien fittings use PLUGH as already specified.

Apply its finite declared improvement to the selected physical component and consume the upgrade item once. Keep accumulated improvements intrinsic to that component; do not retain a second reusable item that can also be sold or fitted elsewhere.

Compare the component's real effective graded statistics with the next compatible grade's authoritative template. On reaching or exceeding all required graded thresholds, promote its item identity/specification to that grade. Merely accumulating an arbitrary number of upgrades or changing a label is insufficient.

Promotion keeps the same instance and provenance, existing compatible features, accumulated stats and receipts. It must not reset improvements, refill shields/fuel, create ammunition or charge the shop price of the new item.

Carry excess improvements forward toward the next grade. One large upgrade may cross several thresholds; resolve this deterministically once, with one concise final promotion notification and full history records.

If the upgrade improves only a non-grading feature, preserve that real improvement but do not falsely claim that all next-grade statistics are met. Show which threshold remains. Specialty capabilities retain their module/ownership requirements.

At Elite use an explicitly defined terminal family envelope and allow only compatible feature/axis improvements within its declared limits. Display maximum grade and cap details; do not create unnamed levels or allow unlimited compounding.

authoritative_templates.owner: Elite Coder 1, coordinated with Coder2 item/effect data before the next immutable contract checkpoint
requirements: One shared data authority defines grade names, ordered templates, required axes, bounds, valuation and interpolation for each compatible component family. UI, fitting, simulation, save migration and tests use it.

Next-grade required benefit axes never decrease, and at least one improves. Reverse-cost axes such as heat/energy demand/spool time use lower-is-better thresholds. Optional specialty features do not silently replace required purchased targeting add-ons.

Capacity and recharge are actual shield stats. Grade progress shows both when both are required; a recharge-only upgrade must not pretend capacity increased. Preserve front/rear-specific improvements and require the documented system-level thresholds.

Grade promotion is within a compatible component family. Do not turn a Mining Laser into a combat laser merely because damage crosses a number or remove its extraction specialization. Do not grant separate Mining/Salvage targeting modules from improving computer speed/precision alone.

Replace the earlier generic 30-percent lifetime limit with per-grade/family limits that permit promotion, plus a finite Elite terminal envelope. Once applied, legacy cap rules must not clip already-earned stats during promotion.

Record the concrete monotonic shield table and its trade/upgrade values with the implementation handoff, then publish exact stats in the equipment documentation. Preserve existing item prices/earned rewards unless their change is explicitly necessary and explained as part of progression; do not use raw legacy multipliers as unvalidated thresholds.
authoritative_templates.verified_legacy_problem: Current source LaserKind damage is Pulse=15, Mining=50, Beam=15, Military=23. ShieldBooster computes 1.5 times damage/Pulse, giving legacy multipliers 1.5, 5, 1.5, 2.3 and Capital=6.9. These cannot be used unchanged as an ascending Basic II/Intermediary/Intermediary II/Advanced/Advanced II threshold sequence. Correct the progression table without weakening a saved component's actual stats.
authoritative_templates.migration: Retain exact saved effective stats, upgrades, cargo, cash, legal/mission state, installed module entitlements and Capital earned flag. Derive appropriate progress/grade from the new templates, preserving excess or grandfathered improvements. Never downgrade real strength to match a display category or silently erase earned value. Document label/grade normalization when legacy names and stats disagree.

rewards_and_installation.elite_reward: The existing combat-Elite reward remains the Advanced II module formerly named Capital. Component upgrades can then progress Advanced II into Elite shield grade without requiring a new combat rank or claiming the reward again. Keep actual rank/earned flag separate from equipment quality.
rewards_and_installation.xyzzymode: User's existing maximum-equipment rule means new maximum-grade shield equipment in XYZZY is Elite once this progression is implemented. This grant does not set combat rank, earned reward state or unlimited cash. Do not regress higher-quality saved components.
rewards_and_installation.ship_exchange: Component grade and accumulated intrinsic effects travel with the actual compatible transferred module, not with a globally copied commander bonus. Hull-bound changes remain with their hull. Selling/removing an integrated upgrade cannot produce duplicated component instances or reusable consumed loot.

presentation.equipment_and_status: Basic Shield plus module hierarchy remains. Show the actual current graded component, effective stats, applied improvements and next-grade progress; e.g. Basic II Shield - capacity 420 / next threshold 500, recharge 1.2 / 1.5. Example numbers are illustrative only. At promotion show the new actual item name on every screen.
presentation.fitting: Preview whether the selected upgrade changes grade, which metrics improve, carried excess and remaining thresholds. State any compatibility or cap refusal before consuming the item.
presentation.hud_and_comparisons: HUD normalization, damage/recharge, target disclosure, showroom/trade comparisons, salvage inventory and PLUGH services use the same promoted item and real stats. Maintain fixed small fonts and compact layout.
presentation.voice_and_docs: Display and voice a one-time '<component> upgraded to <grade>' through the existing event queue. Update README, shield/equipment/targeting/salvage/PLUGH guides and in-game help with the full seven-grade ladder, actual thresholds, fit examples, excess carry, family-specific limits, reward/rank distinction and migration. Label pending behaviour until integration ships.

ownership.Elite Coder 1: Authoritative template/stat/promotion/fit/save/migration/valuation integration, UI/docs/voice, shared component-instance ownership. Reconcile old shield damage-ratio progression in the separate gameplay feature, not frozen route release.
ownership.Elite Coder 2: Recovered upgrade item/effect metadata, finite source-weighted loot, component-family/quality/threshold contract review and independent seeded tests. Avoid central shared-file edits; agree immutable template/effect checkpoint with G1.
ownership.Mission researcher: Compatibility review or specifically transferred independent tests when available; preserve mission-specific shield/damage/provenance and reward rules.

acceptance: Upgrade Basic through Basic II, Intermediate, Intermediate II, Advanced, Advanced II and Elite using real finite compatible items; promotion occurs at the declared required stat thresholds.

A below-threshold upgrade changes actual stats and progress but not grade. Exact-threshold, excess, multiple-grade and reverse-cost improvements resolve correctly without loss or duplicate notifications.
Mixed capacity/recharge upgrades show truthful remaining thresholds. Mining/Salvage targeting entitlements and weapon specializations are not accidentally granted/replaced by numeric promotion.
Repeated application/save/reload/failure/retry/transfer cannot compound already-applied effects or clone items. Promotion preserves current shield fraction and finite ammo/fuel.

Legacy non-monotonic booster saves preserve actual strength and earned state through the new table. Component Elite is separate from combat Elite; Advanced II reward is one-time and XYZZY grants maximum hardware independently.
All shops/status/HUD/details/target information/showroom/salvage/PLUGH/voice/docs reflect the same actual graded item and stats. Focused boundary regressions and final integrated make ci pass.
